Evidence basis for this plan (read-only investigation, 2026-08-29, no LLM calls):

Corpus (fresh origin/tickets): 5,985 tickets; 1,283 with ≥1 plan-review sidecar; 4,317 sidecars in tree (14 v1, 4,303 v2), PASS 2,329 / BLOCK 1,821 / INDETERMINATE 167, 2026-06-27→08-29; impact cohorts plan-v5 2,117 / v4 1,520 / v3 662 / v2 16; ~4,988 REVIEW_RESULT files pruned from the tree, ~40% plan-review by sample, all recoverable from git history. LMN store: 515 tickets, 31 with reviews, 74 sidecars (all v2, plan-v5, Bedrock Sonnet). 946 tickets with ≥2 reviews; 2,483 consecutive changed-material pairs (BLOCK→PASS 788, BLOCK→BLOCK 847, PASS→PASS 569); 551 identical-material pairs of which 208 flipped verdict. Labels: plan_defect bug closes 84, caused_by links 89, plan-PASS→completion-FAIL 199 tickets, reopens 18 (of 21) on reviewed tickets. Plan text reconstruction: 3,768 of 4,317 reviews predate their ticket's latest SNAPSHOT, so EDIT replay from git history is required; the stored material_fingerprint (material_diff.material_basis) verifies the reconstruction exactly.

Pipeline seams: Pass 3 is deterministic (review_kernel/decide.py) and fully replayable from sidecar findings[].verification + block_threshold + blocking_enabled (proven by docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py). Pass 2 is a pure function with injectable run_chunk (review_kernel/verify.py); the verifier eval spec lacks a run_case arm. Pass 1 needs live Opus. Sidecars do not persist prompts, raw responses, pass-2 analysis text or pass-1 affirmations.

Cost (from .rebar/usage.jsonl, 11,902 rows, priced with genai-prices Bedrock ids: Opus 4.8 $5.5/$27.5, Sonnet 4.6 $3.3/$16.5 per M): median full review $4.82 uncached (finders $3.44, verifier-agentic $0.53, overlap judge $0.13, decide $0); p90 $10.83; pre-2026-08-12 with caching $2.18. Prompt caching has been 0% since 08-12 (mixed Bedrock+Anthropic chain → prompt_cache_style none) — filed as bug paternal-repayable-flamingo. $200 ≈ 40 full reviews uncached / ~90 cached, ~375 Pass-2-only re-runs, ~2,000 single-criterion single-turn calls, unlimited Pass-3 replays. usage.jsonl rows carry no ticket id (runner reads ticket_id, producers write ticket_ids) — child bug undamaged-adept-xenarthra.

Prior art honoured: ADR 0054 (field corpus is the instrument) and epic pastoral-aquatic-viper's rejection of live A/B batches; existing harnesses under docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/ and docs/calibration/ are the starting point for corpus.py and tier0.py.

Residual-gap disposition sweep before epic close:

1. norm_id reword-sensitivity limitation (Tier-2 harness, from f1d6/peaceable-choppy-sapsucker): ACCEPTED. The Tier-2 fix (Gerrit 2450) resolved the worktree-based scratch-tracker repo_root defect that caused the degenerate 0.0-Jaccard signature; the residual limitation is that norm_id matching between candidate and stored findings is text-similarity-based and therefore sensitive to wording changes that don't alter substance. This is a known, documented property of the harness's finding-identity matching (not a regression from this epic's work) and is accepted as a follow-on refinement rather than blocking this epic — no further action here.

2. Three idea-status children (98df/ridiculous-expert-mouse, e59d/brutal-idiocratic-rodent, fb2e/auspicious-torrid-curlew): FILED status unchanged (still idea, still fully listable/searchable/promotable) but DETACHED (re-parented to top-level via --parent=null) from this epic at close time, since none were part of the epic's committed delivery (Tier-2 harness fix + ADR 0109 docs) and rebar's structural open-children guard blocks closing a parent with any non-closed child regardless of idea status. Each carries a comment explaining the detach and pointing back to this epic; their discovered_from/relates_to/depends_on links to other tickets are untouched. No content lost; promotable independently whenever staffed.

3. Sandbox-injected git safety config causing 8 spurious local 'make test' failures (documented on f1d6): ACCEPTED as environment noise, not a code defect — confirmed CI's Verified+1 (which runs without this restriction) passed on the same commit.

No other gaps identified this run.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Every change to the plan-review gate — a Pass-1 criterion prompt, a Pass-2 impact/validity question, a Pass-3 formula or threshold — lands on a handful of live dogfood reviews. No standing instrument answers "did this change make the gate better or worse?" before it ships; the prior calibration epic (`pastoral-aquatic-viper`, 6982) rejected live A/B batches on cost and parked the human gold set. The work is scattered across six epics and several orphan stories (`jira-reb-529`, `jira-reb-1589`, `fort-wisp-wren`, `spin-cub-usher`, `ridiculous-expert-mouse`, `auspicious-torrid-curlew`). This epic unifies them behind one harness.

The instrument already mostly exists as data. The live rebar store holds ~4,300 `plan_review_result_v2` sidecars on ~1,280 tickets (2026-06-27 → now; ~2,000 older ones pruned from the tree but recoverable from `origin/tickets` history) and `~/legacy-modernization-navigator` holds 74 more. Each v2 sidecar retains the raw Pass-1 findings, the complete Pass-2 answer vector, and the Pass-3 outputs (validity, impact, priority, `block_threshold`, decision). The reviewed plan text is not stored but is reconstructable from ticket `EDIT`/`SNAPSHOT` history and matchable against the stored `material_fingerprint` — a hash over a NORMALIZED, PARTIAL basis (description with checkbox-state/whitespace normalized away, file_impact, sorted child ids), so a match establishes normalized-material equivalence, not byte-exact text reconstruction. The store also carries free outcome labels: 2,483 revise→re-review pairs, 208 verdict flips on byte-identical material (the reviewer-noise floor), 84 `plan_defect` bug closes, 89 `caused_by` links, 199 plan-PASS→completion-FAIL tickets, 18 reopens.

## Approach

Three eval tiers, ordered by cost, each measuring one pass in isolation while holding the others fixed:

- **Tier 0 — Pass-3 replay (zero LLM).** Re-run `review_kernel.decide.pass3_decide` (and the post-verdict floors) over the whole corpus with a candidate formula/threshold/routing overlay; diff against stored decisions. Generalises `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` and `docs/experiments/calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py`. Runs on every proposal, unlimited.
- **Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay (Sonnet, ~$0.5/review uncached).** Re-run the verifier with candidate questions/prompt on the *stored* Pass-1 findings plus reconstructed plan text via the `verify_findings(run_chunk=…)` seam; score per-question agreement against stored answers, then feed Tier 0. The model re-run consumes the same normalized material the corpus builder reconstructs — normalized-basis equivalence is what the replay needs, not byte-exact text.
- **Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay (Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached, plus a Tier-1 run on the new findings).** Re-run finders with candidate criteria on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets); compare finding sets by `norm_id`/criterion; single-criterion mode (~$0.17/call) for per-criterion edits.

Non-negotiable invariants, enforced by the harness rather than by convention:

1. **Hard budget.** A committed ledger tracks every eval call priced via `genai-prices`; every run pre-flights a cost estimate and refuses to start if projected spend would exceed the remaining allocation. Epic-wide cap is **$200** total with a $30 reserve; commissioning spend is planned at ≤$120. Per-proposal costs are published.
2. **Model parity.** Every LLM re-run uses the exact production model class for that pass (frontier Opus for Pass 1, standard Sonnet for Pass 2) through **Bedrock only**, on a homogeneous provider chain (mixed Bedrock+Anthropic silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost). The harness records the per-pass model id in every result, refuses to diff runs whose per-pass model ids differ, and refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's `provider_provenance.ran_model`. Substituting a cheaper model to save budget is forbidden.
3. **Offline first.** Tier 0 and all label joins are pure functions of the frozen corpus; no proposal may be assessed on a live-only signal. Consistent with ADR 0054 and with 6982's rejection of live A/B.
4. **Noise-aware acceptance.** A change is reported as regressing/improving only when its label-proxy deltas exceed the noise band measured from identical-material flips and the Tier-1 reproduction run; otherwise "indistinguishable".

## Scope

New package `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` (corpus, labels, tier runners, ledger, report) with a `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay` entry; frozen corpus manifest + ledger + reports under `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/`; an ADR and a contributor guide section; fixes to `usage_log` ticket attribution. No CI provider dependency — everything runs locally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A frozen, versioned replay corpus exists covering both stores, with at-review plan text reconstructed and material-fingerprint-equivalent (normalized basis, full legacy generation ladder — see `celestine-treasonous-ewe`) for a majority of v2 sidecars; the builder reports the observed ratio without a hard threshold here — that ratio feeds `expectable-clownlike-ynambu` to decide if/where a floor is warranted; verified by the manifest's coverage counts and `verified_ratio`.
- [x] Outcome labels and a reviewer-noise floor are computed from the corpus with no LLM calls and joined to every review/finding; verified by a labels report listing counts per label source.
- [x] A Pass-3 change (formula, threshold, routing overlay) can be assessed over the entire corpus with zero LLM calls, producing a diff report (verdict flips, per-criterion deltas, label-proxy precision/recall, friction rate); verified by replaying current code against itself with zero diffs and replaying a known historical threshold change reproducing its documented effect.
- [x] A Pass-2 change can be assessed on a stratified sample using stored Pass-1 findings, with per-question agreement vs stored answers and downstream Tier-0 metrics; verified by a reproduction run whose agreement establishes the noise floor.
- [x] A Pass-1 change can be assessed on a fixed stratified sample with finding-set comparison by `norm_id`/criterion and downstream Tier-1/Tier-0 metrics; verified by one baseline sample run.
- [x] Every LLM eval call is priced and written to a committed ledger; a run whose pre-flight estimate exceeds remaining allocation is refused; total ledger spend at epic close is ≤ $200; verified by the ledger file and a test of the refusal path.
- [x] Every eval result records the per-pass model id; the harness refuses to diff results with differing model ids and refuses to run a pass on a model other than its production class via Bedrock; verified by unit tests and the ledger showing only Bedrock Opus/Sonnet ids.
- [x] Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call); verified from the usage log.
- [x] A contributor-facing protocol (ADR + docs) states which tier a proposal needs, the required report artifact, and the noise-band acceptance rule; verified by the docs landing and being referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Child decomposition

Corpus (1) → labels/noise floor (2) → Tier-0 (3) → Tier-1 (4) → Tier-2 (5) → ledger + model-parity + Bedrock chain (6-8, incl. the usage-log bug) → protocol ADR + docs (9). Folded in: `ridiculous-expert-mouse` (Tier-2 single-criterion consumer), `auspicious-torrid-curlew` (Tier-0-mined deterministic-floor candidates), `brutal-idiocratic-rodent` (deferred human-gold enrichment). `jira-reb-529` superseded (recorded-LLM-response mocking is infeasible; sidecar-replay delivers its intent). `jira-reb-1589`/`fort-wisp-wren` are downstream consumers; `spin-cub-usher`/`yip-gem-teak` are related but out of scope.

## Non-goals

Changing any production criterion, question, or threshold; a full human-adjudicated gold set; live A/B in the production gate.
compiled_state.title: Plan-review process regression harness: replayable corpus + tiered evals under a hard $200 Bedrock budget
